Surah al-Ma'arij (The Ascending Stairways)
[Meccan, and its verses are forty-four.]

﴿Asked a questioner﴾ (sa'ala sa'il): a caller called for (da'a da'in).
For the disbelievers; there is none to repel it. He is al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, who said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth﴾, and so on, to the end of the verse.
﴿مِن اللَّه﴾ [من الله] متصل بـ"واقع" ﴿ذِي المَعارِج﴾ [ذي المعارج]، أي مَصاعِد المَلائِكَة، وهي السماوات.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 4:

﴿Ascend﴾ (read with ta' and with ya') ﴿the angels and the Spirit﴾, i.e. Jibril, ﴿to Him﴾, i.e. to the place of the descent of His command from the heaven, ﴿in a Day﴾ (this is related to a verb understood, meaning: the punishment will befall them) on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾ with respect to the disbelievers, because of the hardships they encounter in it; as for the believer, it will be lighter for him than an obligatory prayer which he prays in the world, as has come in the hadith.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 5:

﴿So be patient﴾ — and this was before he was commanded to fight — ﴿with a beautiful patience﴾, meaning without impatience (jaza') in it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 6:

﴿Indeed, they see it﴾ i.e., the punishment ﴿as distant﴾, not occurring.
﴿And We see it as near﴾, certainly to occur, without doubt.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 8:

﴿On the day the sky becomes like murky oil﴾ is related to a deleted element whose estimated form is "it will occur." ﴿Like murky oil﴾: like molten silver.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 9:

﴿And the mountains will be like wool﴾, like wool in its lightness and in being carried away by the wind.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿And no intimate friend will ask an intimate friend﴾

Translation of the commentary:

﴿And no intimate friend will ask an intimate friend﴾ — a close relative will not ask his close relative, because each is preoccupied with his own condition.

﴿They will be made to see one another﴾, meaning the close ones (al-ahmaʾ) see each other, recognise one another, and do not speak. The clause is *mustaʾnafa* (a resumptive, independent sentence, not grammatically tied to what precedes it). ﴿The criminal would wish﴾, meaning the disbeliever wishes ﴿if only he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day﴾. Here *law* (لَوْ) carries the meaning of *an* (أنْ, "that"). The verb *yaftadi* (يَفْتَدِي) is read with a kasra and with a fatha on the *meem* (الميم).
﴿And his wife﴾, [i.e.] his spouse.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 13:

﴿And his close kindred⦆ (faṣīlatahu), his clan, so called because he is separated (li-faslihi) from them. ﴿who shelters him⦆ (allatī tu'wīhi), who gathers him in, takes him in.
And whoever is on the earth, all of them, then it (would) save him. That ransom (al-iftida', the ransoming) — and the clause is conjoined to "would ransom himself" (yaftadi).

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 15:

﴿Kalla﴾ (No!) is a rejection of what he desires. ﴿Innaha﴾ (Indeed it), i.e., the Fire, ﴿la-Zaa﴾ (is Laza), a name for Jahannam (Hell), because it blazes (tatalaẓẓā), i.e., it flames fiercely against the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 16:

﴿Plucking out the scalp﴾ (nazzaʿa lil-shawā), the plural of shawāh, which is the skin of the head.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 17:

﴿It calls out to the one who turned his back and withdrew﴾ from faith, by saying: "To me, to me!"

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 18:

﴿And he gathered﴾ the wealth ﴿and hoarded it﴾; he kept it in its container and did not pay the right of God from it.
﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾: a *ḥāl* (circumstantial qualifier) *muqaddara* (anticipated, describing a state that comes about later), and its explanation.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 20:

﴿When evil touches him, he is distressed and impatient﴾ at the time evil touches him.
﴿And when good touches him, he is miserly﴾. At the time good touches him, i.e., wealth, he withholds from it the right of Allah.
﴿Except those who pray﴾, i.e., the believers.

Those who are constant (muwaziboon) in their prayer.

Note on the passage: the Arabic is "﴿الَّذِينَ هُمْ عَلى صَلاتهمْ دائِمُونَ﴾ مُواظِبُونَ", which is the Jalalayn's gloss on the verse with the word "مُواظِبُونَ" (muwazibun, "persevering, keeping to regularly") explaining "دائِمُونَ" (da'imun, "constant").

Translation:

﴿Those who are constant in their prayer﴾ — persevering (muwazibun) in it.

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 24:**

﴿And those in whose wealth there is a known right﴾ is the zakat.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 25:

﴿For the beggar and the deprived.﴾ The one who refrains from asking, so he is deprived.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 26:

﴿And those who affirm the Day of Judgment﴾ the Recompense.
﴿And those who are, concerning the punishment of their Lord, apprehensive﴾ fearful.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 28:

﴿Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not to be deemed safe.﴾ Its descent is not to be deemed safe.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 70, verse 30:

﴿Except from their wives or those their right hands possess﴾ from the slave-women.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 31:

﴿Whoever seeks beyond that, it is they who are the transgressors.﴾ Those who exceed the lawful (ḥalāl) to the unlawful (ḥarām).

Those who are faithful to their trusts (لِأَماناتِهِمْ) and their covenant (وعَهْدهمْ) are keepers (راعُونَ), guarding them.

And in one reading it is recited in the singular (بِالإفْرادِ), i.e. لِأَمانَتِهِمْ: what they have been entrusted with (ما ائْتَمَنُوا عَلَيْهِ) of matters of religion and of the world (مِن أمْر الدِّين والدُّنْيا). "Their covenant" (وعَهْدهمْ) is the pledge that was taken from them (المَأْخُوذ عَلَيْهِمْ) concerning that.

And those who stand firm in their testimonies (﴿والَّذِينَ هُمْ بِشَهاداتِهِمْ﴾ — "And those who, in their testimonies") — and in another reading, with the plural (بِالجَمْعِ, "bi-al-jam'") — ﴿قائِمُونَ﴾ ("are upright") — they uphold them (يُقِيمُونَها) and do not conceal them (ولا يَكْتُمُونَها).

Translation of the Qur'anic text: "And those who are steadfast in their testimonies."

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 34:

﴿And those who are constant in their prayers﴾ by performing them at their appointed times.

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 36:

﴿So what is [the matter] with those who disbelieve, before you﴾, meaning toward you. ﴿Rushing﴾ is a حال (ḥāl, circumstantial accusative), meaning those who keep their gaze fixed (مُدِيمِي النَّظَر, mudīmī al-naẓar).

Translation of the passage:

﴿Off the right and off the left﴾ from you, ﴿in groups﴾ is also a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: gatherings, circle after circle, saying in mockery of the believers: ﴿If these enter the Garden, we will surely enter it before them.﴾

﴿No!﴾ This is a deterrent to them from their greed for Paradise. ﴿Indeed, We created them﴾ like others ﴿from that which they know﴾, from a nutfah (a drop of fluid). So one should not hope for Paradise by this (i.e., by one's lineage or status), but hope for it only through taqwa (God-consciousness, piety).
﴿So no﴾: the lā is extra (zā'idah, a redundant particle). ﴿I swear by the Lord of the easts and the wests﴾, referring to the sun, the moon, and the rest of the stars.

ﷻ "Upon Our power to replace them with better than them, and We are not to be outdone." 

Tafsir al-Jalalayn: ﴿عَلى أنْ نُبَدَّل﴾ (Upon Our power to replace) نَأْتِي بَدَلهمْ (We bring in their place) ﴿خَيْرًا مِنهُمْ﴾ (better than them) ﴿وما نَحْنُ بِمَسْبُوقِينَ﴾ (and We are not to be outdone) بِعاجِزِينَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ (by being unable to do that).

**Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 70, verse 42:**

﴿So leave them﴾ (utrukhum), leave them alone, ﴿to plunge﴾ (yakhudu) into their falsehood, ﴿and to play﴾ (yal'abu) in their worldly life, ﴿until they encounter﴾ (yulaqu), that is, meet, ﴿their Day which they are promised﴾, in which is the punishment.

On the Day they come out from the graves (al-ajdath) swiftly (sira'an) toward the gathering place (al-mahshar), as if they were rushing toward a shrine (ila nusub), and in one reading with both letters vowelled with a ḍammah, [nusub is] a thing set up, like a sign or a banner. [They are] hastening (yuwfidun), that is, they hurry.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 70, verse 44:

﴿Khashi'a﴾ (humbled), ﴿abṣāruhum﴾ (their eyes), ﴿tarhaquhum﴾ (covers them), ﴿dhillah﴾ (with humiliation). ﴿Dhālika al-yawm alladhī kānū yū'adūn﴾ (That is the Day which they were promised).

Dhālika (that) is the subject (mubtada'), and what follows it is the predicate (khabar), and its meaning is the Day of Resurrection.
